question: Can probing be prevented --- a taker submitting requests it never intends to trade on, to read the price envelope for free?
the_design: The taker commits an acceptance level L with the request. The circuit computes the winner as before, then one comparison fill = (key <= L*WIDE + WIDE-1), and returns fill*key under the trader's mask. A quote at or inside the level is a trade.

binding_limit_below_the_quote.note: the taker removes its own mask and gets zero. It learns the fill bit and nothing else --- which is the property the whole design rests on, so it is measured rather than argued.

predictions.why: Both misses have one cause. The tournament's comparisons run 16 wide per layer and amortise; the fill comparison is a single standalone one paying full depth and full per-comparison cost. The estimate priced it as though it joined the batch.
predictions.the_optimisation_that_follows: fold the fill comparison into the last tournament layer so it shares the batch. Not done, and it should take most of the nine rounds back.

what_it_actually_buys.not: It does not stop probing, and saying so would be wrong.
what_it_actually_buys.the_asymmetry: A prober can raise L from below and learn `worse than this` each time for free, converging on the quote from underneath. What costs a trade is learning the market is BETTER than a stated level --- because that is a fill.
what_it_actually_buys.the_ceiling_it_reaches: A resting limit order in a public book says the same thing: I will trade at L, and not being filled says the market is worse. So a binding-limit RFQ leaks no more than a central limit order book, and less, because L is committed rather than displayed. run_clob_baseline.py already measures that baseline.
what_it_actually_buys.bisection_costs_fills: Binary search terminates on the first `q <= L`, which is a fill. Against a uniform q the first midpoint probe fills with probability 1/2, so a prober cannot bisect without trading about half the time. Only the linear crawl from below stays free, and it needs range/step requests --- which a venue can rate-limit or charge for.

why_the_fill_bit_is_masked_too: Revealing fill in the clear would say which slots traded, and that is exactly what the is_real cover traffic exists to hide: a public fill bit marks every cover slot as cover. So it comes back under a second trader mask.
the_open_part: Binding needs settlement the taker cannot decline, and the quorum cannot see the fill bit it would be settling on. The shape is that the quorum signs an instruction carrying a COMMITMENT to fill, and DeFMI requires a proof that fill = 1 before it moves anything --- but who can produce that proof, and what stops a taker sitting on it, is not resolved here. Collateral escrowed in advance is necessary and probably not sufficient.
the_cost_to_an_honest_taker: Giving up the right to decline after seeing the price is giving up last look --- which is what makes probing possible, and what the FX Global Code spent years constraining. It is aligned with where the regulation went and it is still a real cost: a binding level is exposed to being filled on a stale quote, which is what the 26-second staleness measurement is about.
